segments.say: Now that your body is soft and still, let's think, very gently, about all the unfinished things in your life. The projects you haven't started. The ideas you haven't had yet. The problems that don't have answers. Usually, these can feel like weights. But tonight, let's look at them a little differently. Not as failures. As seeds.

Think of a garden in winter. On the surface, nothing much is happening. The soil looks bare. But underneath, seeds are resting, waiting for their time. They don't need to be pulled up and checked every day. They don't need to be hurried. They simply need time, and darkness, and a little patience. Your unfinished ideas might be just like that.

Remember Mira's three weeks of sketches. At the time, they felt like failure. Fox after fox, lighthouse after lighthouse, nothing working. But they were seeds. Each one put something into the soil of her mind. And when the time came, in the warmth of the shower, they came up together, as a girl with jars of sounds.

So here's a kind thought to rest with. Nothing you tried was wasted. Every attempt, every rough draft, every idea that didn't quite work, went somewhere. It became part of what you know, part of what your mind can draw on later. Even the things that seemed to lead nowhere were quietly preparing the ground for something else.

Picture a garden at twilight in late winter. Neat wooden beds of dark soil. And here and there, if you look closely, the tiniest green shoots, just beginning to break through. Most of the seeds aren't ready yet. That's fine. They'll come up when they're ready, each in its own season. There's no need to dig them up and check.

You don't need to force your ideas tonight. You can trust them to grow in the dark, the way seeds do. Some will come up tomorrow. Some will come up next month, or next year, in a shower, on a walk, at the edge of sleep. And some will never come up at all, and that's alright too. The garden is wide. There's room for all of it.

Let yourself be kind to your own mind tonight. It has worked hard today, even if it didn't feel like it. It has noticed things, remembered things, worried about things, and quietly connected things you'll never know about. It deserves to rest now. There's nothing more it needs to produce. No more ideas required.

Here are some things that are allowed tonight. Not knowing. Being stuck. Leaving things unfinished. Resting instead of trying. All of these are allowed. None of them mean you're doing anything wrong. They're simply part of how a mind works, how ideas grow, how people live. You can let yourself have all of them, without any guilt at all.

Imagine, for a moment, a quiet house at night. Mira's house, perhaps, or your own. The rooms are dark. The kettle is cold. The stairs creak softly now and then, settling as the house cools. The windows hold the last faint glow of the street. Everyone inside is asleep, or nearly asleep, and the house holds them all, patiently, until morning.

And listen, in your imagination, to the small sounds of a sleeping house. The tick of a clock. The hum of the fridge downstairs. The soft sigh of wind against the window. Rain beginning, very lightly, on the roof. If Mira were awake, she might collect these sounds in her jars. But tonight, they simply drift past, soft and kind, and fade.

Let's stay with the rain for a moment. It's falling softly now, tapping on the roof, trickling down the windows. A steady, gentle sound. Not a storm. Just a quiet rain, the kind that makes a warm bed feel even warmer. Each drop is small. Together, they make a sound like a long, slow breath, going on and on into the night.

Here's another small thought for the dark. The rain doesn't hurry. Neither do you. It simply falls, at its own pace, without needing to get anywhere. You can rest like that, too. At your own pace. Without needing to be anywhere else, or anyone else, or to have done anything more than you've already done.

show.text: The rain doesn't hurry. Neither do you.

segments.say: If you'd like, let a little gratitude come into the quiet. Not for anything grand. Just for ordinary things. A warm bed. A roof over the rain. A body that knows how to breathe. A mind that, given time, knows how to find its way to new ideas. These ordinary things are quite remarkable, when you stop to notice them.

You might notice your thoughts becoming a little looser now. Images sliding into one another. A jar, a stream, a meadow, a creaking stair. That's the doorway to sleep, opening gently. There's nothing you need to catch. No bottle to drop. Just let yourself drift towards it, as slowly as you like, and step through whenever you're ready.

For now, all is well. The house is quiet. The rain is soft. The garden is resting. The jars are on the shelf. Your body is heavy and warm. Your mind is free to wander, or to rest. There's nowhere else you need to be. This moment, this quiet moment, is enough. It's more than enough.

Let's say it once more, slowly. The house is quiet. The rain is soft. The jars are on the shelf. Your body is resting. Each of these is true, right now, in this moment. There's nothing to add to them, and nothing to take away. Just let them settle around you, like a warm blanket, as the night goes on.

show.title: All is well
items: The jars are on the shelf

segments.say: In a little while, we'll say goodnight. But there's no need to wait for it. If sleep comes now, let it come. If you're still listening, that's lovely too. Just keep breathing slowly, in and out, letting the rain keep its gentle time, and letting yourself sink, softly, a little deeper into rest.
